Subject: MSA redlines: private deployment license contingencies & evidence routing

Marissa —

Thanks for the demo last week. Attached are HealthSync's redlines to the MSA and proposed Order Form that cover private (VPC/on-prem) deployment options. Two items we need clarity on before we can move to legal approval:

1) License contingency: we want an explicit fallback if Redwood cannot deliver operator-attested witness support within the proposed window — equivalent to an escrow-like snapshot deposit. Please point to where that pathway exists in the contract or propose language.

2) Evidence & audit routing: HealthSync requires a predictable route for forensic snapshots and a clear handoff process for keys (KMS) and logs. Our security team flagged lack of detail on custody transfer and time-to-witness.

Attached: HealthSync_MSA_redlines_20280725.docx (redline)

Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a sealed snapshot deposit model vs witness certification? If neither, what alternative remediation guarantees can you offer?

We'd like to wrap this prior to procurement's Q3 board review (target: first week of August).

Best,
Eleanor Park
Sr. Counsel, HealthSync

Eleanor —

Thanks for sending the redlines and the clear ask. We can get this scoped quickly. High-level response:

• We support both a witnessed-snapshot workflow (Redwood personnel witness and sign attestation) and a sealed-snapshot deposit model (snapshot encrypted to a mutually-agreed escrow steward). We usually prefer witnessed for faster validation but can do sealed deposit for jurisdictional constraints.

• Key custody options: integration with customer KMS (preferred for clients who control keys) or Redwood-managed sealed key escrow (HSM-backed) with audited access.

Next steps I propose: Ben (legal) will propose narrow MSA language to capture both pathways with a clear trigger and remedy. David (ops) will provide a short attachment describing the witness vs sealed-deposit procedures and timelines.

I'll target an internal reply with language and the ops note by EOD Wednesday (Jul 26). Is a live 30-minute sync Thursday helpful for final alignment?

Thanks — looping you in.

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer GTM, Redwood Inference

Marissa / David —

Thanks Eleanor — useful framing. A few legal priorities from our side and suggested guardrails to avoid open-ended exposure:

1) Remedy trigger: define a concrete SLA window (e.g., Redwood to provide witnessed access or sealed deposit within 30 business days of written request) and an explicit remediation (temporary license continuation or credit) if the trigger is missed. Avoid ambiguous language like "reasonable efforts."

2) Scope of deliverables: limit forensic snapshot to the runtime image, configuration manifests, and metadata/epoch logs (no customer data export beyond what is required). If HealthSync insists on broader artifacts, add a narrow, jointly-scoped discovery process.

3) Escrow steward: if sealed-deposit is used, require an independent third-party steward with defined access conditions. We should avoid escrow setups where Redwood has unilateral mindshare over key release.

I'll draft redline snippets that implement the SLA window, the limited artifact scope, and a two-option custody model (Customer-KMS OR third-party escrow steward). David — please include the ops note with estimated time-to-witness, snapshot size expectations, and a short checklist for on-prem validation.

Ben
General Counsel, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Ben / Marissa / Eleanor —

Attaching a short ops note (snapshot-handoff-protocol_v1.pdf) but summarizing key points here:

• Witnessed snapshot (preferred): Redwood ops travels (or connects via secure witness session) to validate snapshot creation and signs an attestation certificate. Typical timeline: 3-7 business days from access approval for VPC; 7-12 business days for on-prem depending on site access. Snapshot size typically 10–80GB depending on model and retention settings.

• Sealed snapshot deposit (escrow): Redwood will produce an encrypted snapshot (AES-256) sealed to a steward public key. Steward only decrypts under contractually defined trigger (mutual consent or arbitration). Timeline: 5–12 business days to produce and transmit to steward.

• KMS options: 1) Customer-managed KMS integration (preferred) — no Redwood-held keys; 2) Redwood HSM-backed escrow with strict audit hooks (temporary decrypt only under specified triggers).

• Access controls: all artifact transfers logged, parity hashes provided, and a post-handoff validation checklist executed with customer security (checksums, bootstrap tests).

Operational ask: please confirm which model (witness vs sealed deposit) HealthSync prefers and whether the steward must be a named third party (we can propose a short vetted list). Also confirm any export-control or regional data boundaries that would affect handoff.

Attachments: snapshot-handoff-protocol_v1.pdf

Marissa / Ben / David —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the two-path approach — that addresses the security team's primary concern. A few confirmations from HealthSync side:

• We prefer the sealed-deposit option for our on-prem nodes due to internal change-control policies. Steward must be an independent third party; please propose a short list.

• SLA window: 30 business days for Redwood to produce and hand off (witness or sealed deposit) is acceptable. Please include a remediation credit equal to one month of service if the SLA is missed; procurement will take that to their finance review.

• Artifact scope: runtime image + configuration manifests + epoch logs is acceptable. We will not request broader PII or data exports.

Requests: can Redwood produce an updated MSA redline that: 1) includes the two-option custody model, 2) defines the 30-business-day SLA trigger and the one-month credit remedy, and 3) references the snapshot-handoff-protocol_v1.pdf as an operational exhibit?

If you can get a redline and DocuSign-ready Order Form to procurement by COB Monday (Jul 30) we'll start internal signoff and schedule a witness window for the week of Aug 6 (sealed-deposit prep window).

Thanks —
Eleanor Park
Sr. Counsel, HealthSync
